full_judgment:
15. But, it may be noticed that the finding as to the genuineness of the contract vide Ext. 1 is not concurrent. The lower appellate court has differed with the finding of the trial court and reversed the same. Now, the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant is that the finding and decision of the court of appeal below are not proper finding and decision of reversal. 

 16. Let me see how far the contention of the learned Advocate is correct. From the analysis of the evidence on record, it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge failed to consider the material particulars of the evidence on behalf of the plaintiff to the effect that not only 1,500/- Taka, but also Taka 500/- more was paid earlier to the executant late Sarat Chandra Sarkar that means according to the contract, out of the total consideration of TK. 2500/-, the executant Late Sarat Chandra Sarkar defendant no. 1 received Tk. 2,000/- in all from he plaintiff and executed the deed of contract Ext. 1. The P. Ws. who had no enmity with the defendants categorically stated that on receipt of the consideration money of Tk. 2,000/- from the plaintiff, the defendant no. 1 Sarat Chandra Sarkar executed the bainapatra Ext. 1. i.e. deed of contract; but the lower appellate court through misconception and misreading of the evidence on record wrongly and arbitrarily disbelieved the story of payment of the said consideration money of Tk. 2,000/- to the executant Sarat Chandra Sarkar before the execution of the deed of contract in question and thereby committed serious illegality in deciding the genuineness of the deed of contract Ext. and as a result there has been a failure of justice. The finding of the lower appellate court reversing that of the trial court on question of genuineness of the deed of contract Ext. 1 is not at all a proer finding of reversal based on any sound reasoning and proper consideration of the evidence on record. The above finding of the lower appellate court appears have been arrived at due to non- consideration as well as misreading of the material piece of evidence. Hence, the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge as to the genuineness of the bainapatra Ext. I is wholly incorrectly and illegal. As such the decision based on such an illegal and arbitrary finding can not be sustained in law. However, it seems to me that the trial-court rightly found the deed of contract Ext. 1 as a genuine one for sale of the land in question of the defendant no.1 late Sarat Chandra Sarkar to the plaintiff and the contract vide Ext. 1 appears to have been duly entered into and genuinely executed by the vendor defendant no.1 on receipt of the earnest money as mentioned above. The trial court appears to have correctly found the same as a genuine and lawful one and accordingly decreed the suit for its enforcement through the specific performance of the contract as prayed for subject to the encumbrance created by Ext. A(1). The finding of the court of appeal below as to the genuineness and validity of the contract Ext. 1 does not appear to be a proper finding of reversal. Hence, the same is liable to be set aside in the interest of justice. In the instant case it is however interesting to note that on the death of the contesting defenant no.1 out of the substituted defendants only defendant 1(kha) and the added defendant no.2 contested the suit and the others did not, again as against the trial court's decree in favour of the plaintiff as against all the defendants, only the added defendant no.2, the present respondent No. 1 SK. Hemayet Hossain @ Ali preference the appeal and his case was that he purchased the suit-land from the defendant no.1 late Sarat Chandra Sarkar vide Ext. 4(1) dated 4.7.69 for a valuable consideration of Tk. 3,000/- without the knowledge of notice of the said deed of contract Ext. 1. Now, when except defendant No. 2, the other defendants had not challenged the decree of the trial court by preferring any appeal, the said decree stands binding on them and as to the gunuinenes of the deed of contract Ext. 1, the defendant no. 2, who claimed to have purchased the suit-land for valuable consideration without knowledge and notice of the contract, was not supposed to know or say anything about the execution and genuineness of the said deed of contract Ext. 1. However, it seems that the lower appellate court without proper application to his judicial mind to the evidence on record, in fact through mistaken assumption of facts and misreading and non-consideration of some material piece of evidence most illegally and arbitrarily held that the bainapatra i.e. deed of contract Ext. 1 was not a genuine one and on such finding reversed the decision of the trial court resulting in a serious miscarriage of justice. Now, in this court, the contesting defendant no.2 is the respondent no.1 but as has been stated above, on one has come to appear to represent him in this court in spite of due service of notice upon him and with regard to the other respondents, the Contesting defendant No.1 (kha) did neither prefer any appeal in the court of appeal below nor as respondent no. 3 (kha) did appear in this court to contest present appeal, though the suit was decreed against him also by the trial court. So far the other 2 respondent nos. 2, 1(ka) and 4(Gha) they did not either contest the suit or prefer aliy appeal against the trial courts decree, but now they have recently appointed M/S. Md. Wahidullah and another as their Advocates to contest the present second appeal and to question the legality of the trial court's decree, which is not permissible in law as they did not either contest the suit or file any appeal against the trial court's decree.
